places.name: Karnak Temple Complex
places.ai_summary: A vast open-air museum and the largest ancient religious site in the world, dedicated to the Theban triad.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited early morning to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Don’t miss the Hypostyle Hall with its massive columns.

attribution.author: Diego Delso

places.name: Luxor Temple
places.ai_summary: A stunning temple complex located on the east bank of the Nile, known for its grand colonnades and statues.

opening_hours.notes: Illuminated at night for a magical experience.

places.place_tip: Visit at night to see the temple beautifully lit.

attribution.title: Paris, Obelisk in the Place de la Concorde, July 22, 2008
attribution.author: Craig Booth from Leiden, Netherlands

places.name: Valley of the Kings
places.ai_summary: A royal burial ground for pharaohs and nobles, featuring elaborately decorated tombs.

opening_hours.notes: Photography inside tombs may require an additional fee.

places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes as there’s a lot of walking involved.
places.address: Valley of the Kings, Luxor, Egypt

places.name: Valley of the Queens
places.ai_summary: The burial site of royal wives, featuring beautiful tombs with intricate decorations.

opening_hours.notes: Less crowded than the Valley of the Kings, offering a more peaceful visit.

places.place_tip: Look out for the tomb of Queen Nefertari, one of the most beautiful in Egypt.
places.address: Valley of the Queens, Luxor, Egypt

attribution.title: Valley of the Queens by Zureks
attribution.author: Zureks
attribution.description: Valley of the Queens as seen from a balloon flight (Luxor, Egypt). The visible road leads to the Valley.

places.name: Temple of Hatshepsut (Deir el-Bahari)
places.ai_summary: A mortuary temple dedicated to Queen Hatshepsut, known for its stunning architecture and terraces.

opening_hours.notes: The temple is best viewed in the morning light.

places.place_tip: Don’t miss the beautiful reliefs and the statue of Hatshepsut.

attribution.title: Templo funerario de Hatshepsut, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 13
attribution.author: Diego Delso
attribution.description: Aerial view during sunrise of the Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut, Luxor, Egypt. The mortuary temple built during the reign of Pharaoh Hatshepsut of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt. The temple is considered to be a masterpiece of ancient architecture. Its three massive terraces rise above the desert floor and into the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari. Her tomb, KV20, lies inside the same massif capped by El Qurn, a pyramid for her mortuary complex. Across the river Nile, the whole structure points towards the monumental Eighth Pylon, Hatshepsut's most recognizable addition to the Temple of Karnak and the site from which the procession of the Beautiful Festival of the Valley departed.

places.name: Colossi of Memnon
places.ai_summary: Two massive stone statues of Pharaoh Amenhotep III, standing guard at the entrance of his mortuary temple.

opening_hours.notes: Best viewed at sunrise when the statues are illuminated.

places.place_tip: Climb up the hill for a better view and fewer crowds.

attribution.title: Colossi of Memnon May 2015 2
attribution.author: MusikAnimal
attribution.description: The Colossi of Memnon in Luxor

places.name: Medinet Habu (Ramses III Temple)
places.ai_summary: A well-preserved temple complex from the reign of Ramses III, featuring impressive reliefs and hieroglyphs.

opening_hours.notes: Less crowded than other temples, offering a more intimate experience.

places.place_tip: Explore the temple's interior for detailed reliefs and the impressive mortuary temple of Ramses III.

attribution.title: Templo funerario de Ramsés III, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 22
attribution.author: Diego Delso
attribution.description: Mortuary temple of Ramses III, Luxor, Egypt

places.name: Ramesseum
places.ai_summary: The mortuary temple of Pharaoh Ramses II, known for its massive statues and impressive architecture.

opening_hours.notes: Look out for the fallen statue of Ramses II, one of the largest in Egypt.

places.place_tip: Visit the site of the famous Colossi of Memnon nearby.

places.name: Luxor Museum
places.ai_summary: A modern museum showcasing artifacts from ancient Thebes, including mummies, statues, and jewelry.

opening_hours.notes: Plan at least 2 hours for your visit to see all exhibits.

places.place_tip: Don’t miss the mummified remains of ancient Egyptians and the impressive collection of artifacts.

attribution.title: Luxor (870133356)
attribution.author: Rob Young from United Kingdom

places.name: Mummification Museum
places.ai_summary: A unique museum dedicated to the ancient Egyptian art of mummification, with exhibits and demonstrations.

opening_hours.notes: Combine your visit with the Luxor Museum as they are close to each other.

places.place_tip: Watch out for the interactive exhibits that explain the mummification process.

places.name: Deir el-Medina (Artisans’ Village)
places.ai_summary: The ancient village of the artisans who worked on the tombs in the Valley of the Kings, with well-preserved ruins.

opening_hours.notes: A guided tour is recommended to fully appreciate the site.

places.place_tip: Explore the remains of the houses, streets, and the communal bakery.

places.name: Tombs of the Nobles (Sheikh Abd el-Qurna)
places.ai_summary: The burial site of nobles and high officials, featuring beautifully decorated tombs.

opening_hours.notes: Less crowded than the Valley of the Kings, offering a more intimate experience.

places.place_tip: Look out for the tomb of Iriney, known for its vibrant colors and intricate carvings.

attribution.title: Tomb TT3 of Pashedu (Kairoinfo4u)
attribution.author: kairoinfo4u
attribution.description: A view of the well preserved and beautifully painted Tomb TT3 from Deir el-Medina on the West Bank of Luxor. This scene depicts the god Osiris with the Mountains of the West behind him. It belonged to Pashedu who served as an Ancient Egyptian artist and foreman at Deir el-Medina under pharaoh Seti I.

places.name: Hot-Air Balloon over West Bank
places.ai_summary: A popular activity offering a bird's-eye view of Luxor's ancient sites and the Nile River.

opening_hours.notes: Weather permitting. Book in advance as it’s a popular activity.

places.place_tip: Bring a camera to capture the stunning views from above.

places.name: Howard Carter House
places.ai_summary: The former home of the famous archaeologist Howard Carter, who discovered the tomb of Tutankhamun.

opening_hours.notes: A small but interesting museum, combine with a visit to the nearby Valley of the Kings.

places.place_tip: See the original artifacts found in Tutankhamun's tomb and learn about Howard Carter's life.

attribution.title: Howard carter
attribution.author: Chicago Daily News, Inc., photographer
attribution.description: Informal portrait of Howard Carter (the archaeologist) standing with a book in his hand next to a train at a station in Chicago, Illinois.

places.name: Felucca to Banana Island
places.ai_summary: A relaxing boat trip on the Nile to Banana Island, known for its lush vegetation and banana plantations.

opening_hours.notes: Best enjoyed in the late afternoon to catch the sunset.

places.place_tip: Take a stroll on Banana Island and enjoy the contrast of greenery with the desert landscape.

places.name: Avenue of Sphinxes Walk
places.ai_summary: A historic walkway lined with sphinx statues, connecting Karnak Temple and Luxor Temple.

opening_hours.notes: Best walked in the early morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat.

places.place_tip: Look for the hieroglyphs and carvings on the sphinxes and nearby walls.

places.name: Abydos Temple (day trip)
places.ai_summary: The temple complex of Abydos, one of the oldest and most important religious sites in ancient Egypt.

opening_hours.notes: A guided tour is recommended due to the site's historical significance.

places.place_tip: Don’t miss the Osireion, a mysterious and ancient structure within the temple complex.

places.name: Dendera Temple (day trip)
places.ai_summary: The well-preserved temple complex of Dendera, dedicated to the goddess Hathor.

opening_hours.notes: The temple is famous for its astronomical ceiling and well-preserved reliefs.

places.place_tip: Take your time to explore the hypostyle hall and the sacred lake.

places.name: Karnak Sound & Light Show
places.ai_summary: An evening sound and light show at the Karnak Temple, depicting the history of Thebes.

opening_hours.notes: The show is available in multiple languages, check schedule in advance.

places.place_tip: Arrive early to find a good seat and enjoy the temple illuminated at night.

places.name: Nile Corniche Promenade
places.ai_summary: A scenic waterfront promenade along the Nile River, perfect for a leisurely stroll or felucca ride.

opening_hours.notes: Best enjoyed in the early morning or late afternoon.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a felucca ride on the Nile for a different perspective of Luxor.
